correctness.rationale: Derived P by multiplying the original dielectric equation by z(z-t)², and verified P(0)=-ut² and P(t)=-4t² so no spurious roots occur for u,t>0. Independently factored disc_z P=4t²Q and disc_t Q=-629856u(2u-1)³. For 0<u<1/4 Q has three real roots with negative product, positive sum, positive Q(0), and Q(2(1-u))<0: one negative and precisely two positive. For 1/4<u<1/2, Q(-1/2)<0<Q(-u) and Q(0)<0 ensure two negative and one positive root; at u=1/2 double negative root, above u=1/2 a single real positive root, at u=1/4 t=0 is excluded. For Q<0, cubic P has one positive real and a conjugate nonreal z pair, whose square roots give two growing oscillatory ω. For Q>0, real-root sign uses positive sum/product and sign of t[t+2(u-1)]: negative means one positive/two negative z, positive means three positive z. Boundary continuity identifies negative and positive double roots. IFT at (u,t)=(1/4,0), quadratic degeneracy near (u,t)=(0,2), and Q_{1/4} factorization establish the reported asymptotics and cutoff. All key symbolic identities plus exact rational u root counts for ten values and 23 independently sampled root-type cases were rechecked in independent_plasma_checks.py; finite checks are not the unrestricted proof. Degenerate real cutoffs can support secular growth.

value.rationale: The symmetric three-electron cold longitudinal dispersion is a physically motivated multistream model. Its exact all-density split between nonoscillatory and oscillatory temporal growth, sharp finite-wavenumber transition ratio b/a=1/4, and singular square-root opening at dilute background distinguish two instability mechanisms and provide quantitative boundaries for further plasma stability comparisons. Although cubic discriminants and qualitative standing/travelling modes are classical, the complete natural one-parameter phase classification and endpoint scaling are non-arbitrary and useful mathematical invariants rather than a random numerical slice or routine normalization check. Does not claim kinetic or nonlinear physics.

final_claim: For every u=b/a>0 and t=(kV)^2/a>0, with equal cold electron populations at velocities ±V and stationary population at 0, the real-coefficient z=ω²/a cubic P=z³-(2t+2+u)z²+[t²+2(u-1)t]z-ut² has discriminant 4t²Q_u(t). For 0<u<1/4, Q has two positive simple zeros t_-<t_+, with two distinct pure-imaginary growing ω for 0<t<t_-, two oscillatory growing ω for t_-<t<t_+, and no Im ω>0 for t>t_+. For u>=1/4 there is one positive t_+, oscillatory growth for 0<t<t_+, and no exponentially growing ω above it. At t_- a repeated imaginary growing root remains; at t_+ repeated real roots may lead to algebraic growth. The boundaries satisfy t_±=2±2√6√u+O(u), t_-=3(1/4-u)+O((1/4-u)²), and t_+(1/4)=(9+6√3)/4.
limitations: Ideal cold collisionless longitudinal temporal modes only, fixed neutralizing ions, k>0, a,b,V>0. No finite-temperature, electromagnetic, spatial convective/absolute, nonlinear, or global-time stability conclusion.
At upper cutoff the real repeated eigenfrequency is not guaranteed semisimple, so algebraic temporal growth remains possible.
